entry: Chinese royal dynasty of the 2nd millennium BC that ruled the Yellow River valley, traditionally succeeding the [[Xia dynasty]] and followed by the [[Zhou dynasty|Western Zhou dynasty]]. Modern scholarship dates it between the 16th and 11th centuries BC. It is the earliest dynasty in traditional Chinese history firmly supported by archaeological evidence. Excavations at Yinxu, near modern Anyang and the final Shang capital of Yin, have revealed royal tombs, palace foundations, and the remains of humans and animals sacrificed in state rituals. The site has also yielded the earliest known Chinese writing, mostly [[Divination|divination]] texts inscribed on oracle bones. More than 20,000 oracle bones were discovered in the 1920s and 1930s, and the inscriptions shed light on politics, economy and religious practice.

[[China|Chinese]] municipality on the southern estuary of the [[Yangtze]] River, the most populous city in China (urban pop., 2026: 30,050,000). Originally a fishing village and market town, Shanghai grew to prominence in the 19th century through trade and its port location. It was one of five treaty ports forced open to European trade after the [[First Opium War]], and the International Settlement and French Concession were established there. It became a primary commercial and financial hub of Asia in the 1930s. Its influence declined during the [[Cold War]], when trade was largely limited to the [[Eastern Bloc]]. Reform and opening up, led by [[Deng Xiaoping]], brought redevelopment from the 1990s and the return of finance and foreign investment. The city is home to the [[Stock exchange|Shanghai Stock Exchange]], the largest in the Asia-Pacific region by market capitalization, and its port is the world's busiest container port.

Main international airport serving [[Shanghai]], China. Construction of its first phase began in 1997, and it opened on September 16, 1999, replacing Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport as the city's primary airport. Located about 30 km east of the city center, it occupies 40 square kilometers beside the coastline. It is the main hub of China Eastern Airlines and a major international hub for Air China, and it is the busiest international gateway in mainland China. It served 84,994,548 passengers in 2025, making it the busiest airport in China and the fifth-busiest in the world.

Canadian singer and songwriter, called the "Queen of Country Pop." She has sold more than 100 million records. Her album *Come On Over* (1997) sold more than 40 million copies, the best-selling studio album by a female solo artist. Following a 2004 hiatus, during which diagnoses of [[Lyme disease]] and dysphonia weakened her voice, she returned with *Now* (2017), which reached number one on the U.S. Billboard 200. She has received five [[Grammy Awards]].

Form of an object, defined by its external boundary, outline or surface and distinct from its color, texture or material. In [[Geometry]], shape excludes an object's position, size, orientation and chirality. A plane shape is constrained to lie on a plane, in contrast to solid three-dimensional shapes. Simple shapes include [[Polygon|polygons]] such as [[Triangle|triangles]], [[Quadrilateral|quadrilaterals]] and pentagons, as well as points, lines, planes and [[Conic section|conic sections]] such as ellipses, circles and parabolas. Common three-dimensional shapes include [[Polyhedron|polyhedra]], ellipsoids, cylinders and cones. Two objects are congruent if one can be moved onto the other by rotations, translations and reflections, and similar if uniform scaling is also allowed.

Local geometry and global topology of the [[Universe|universe]]. Local geometry is defined mainly by spatial curvature, which general relativity relates to gravity. Observations by WMAP, BOOMERanG and Planck show the observable universe is spatially flat to within a 0.4% margin of error. Its global topology is unknown: a multiply connected [[Torus|3-torus]] has zero curvature but is finite, whereas simply connected [[Euclidean space]] is infinite. The observable universe is a roughly spherical region extending about 46 billion [[Light-year|light-years]] in every direction, so its relation to the entire universe is unclear.

American former professional [[Basketball|basketball]] player and sports analyst. A 7-foot-1-inch center, he played for six teams over 19 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). The Orlando Magic made him the first overall pick in the 1992 draft, and he was named NBA Rookie of the Year in 1992–93. He won three championships with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2000, 2001 and 2002, and a fourth with the Miami Heat in 2006. He was the 2000 NBA MVP and a three-time NBA Finals MVP, and is widely regarded as one of the most dominant centers in NBA history.

Body of [[Islam|Islamic]] religious law based on the [[Quran]] and [[Hadith]]. In Islamic terminology, Sharia is the immutable divine law, in contrast to [[Fiqh|fiqh]], the interpretations of Islamic scholars. Traditional jurisprudence recognizes four sources: the Quran, the sunnah, consensus and analogical reasoning. It distinguishes rituals from social dealings, including family law, commercial law and [[Criminal law|criminal law]]. Legal schools of Sunni Islam, such as the Hanafi and Maliki, developed methods for deriving rulings. Most Muslim-majority states retain Sharia largely in family law and penalties, and Islamic movements since the late 20th century have called for full implementation, including hudud punishments such as stoning. Modernists argue it can be brought into line with [[Human rights|human rights]], [[Democracy|democracy]] and [[Women's rights|women's rights]], while fundamentalists advocate its uncompromising application. Several practices have been deemed incompatible with human rights, gender equality and freedom of expression.

Predatory [[Chondrichthyes|cartilaginous fish]] with a ribless endoskeleton, dermal denticles and five to seven gill slits. Modern sharks form the division Selachii, the sister group to the [[Batomorphi]] (rays and skates). Sharks range from the dwarf lanternshark, 17 centimeters long, to the [[Whale shark]], the largest fish in the world, reaching 12 to 18.8 meters. They are found in all seas, to depths of 2,000 meters, and a few species, such as the [[Bull shark]], also tolerate freshwater. Several species, including the [[Great white shark]], [[Tiger shark]] and [[Hammerhead shark]], are apex predators. Shark-like chondrichthyans first appeared in the [[Devonian]] period, and the earliest confirmed modern sharks date to the Early Jurassic, about 200 million years ago. Since 1970, shark populations have been reduced by 71%, mostly by overfishing and finning.

Indian actress, active in Bengali and [[Hindi]] films for more than six decades. She debuted at age 14 in [[Satyajit Ray]]'s *The World of Apu* (1959) and went on to appear in several of his films. She won the Filmfare Award for Best Actress for *Aradhana* and the National Film Award for Best Actress for *Mausam*. She chaired the Central Board of Film Certification from 2004 to 2011. Related to the Nobel laureate [[Rabindranath Tagore]], she received India's Padma Bhushan in 2013.

American actress known for playing femmes fatales and women of mystery in film and television. She became one of the most popular [[Sex symbol|sex symbols]] of the 1990s after playing Catherine Tramell in *Basic Instinct* (1992), for which she earned her first Golden Globe nomination. Her performance as a trophy wife in [[Martin Scorsese]]'s *Casino* (1995) won a Golden Globe and an Academy Award nomination. Her film debut was as an extra in [[Woody Allen]]'s *Stardust Memories* (1980). She won a Primetime Emmy Award for a guest role in *The Practice*.

American actress and model, hailed in the 1960s as one of Hollywood's most promising newcomers and compared favorably with [[Marilyn Monroe]]. Her first major role was as Jennifer North in *Valley of the Dolls* (1967), which earned her a Golden Globe nomination. She became a rising sex symbol after a *Playboy* photoshoot by filmmaker [[Roman Polanski]], whom she went on to marry. She appeared in his *The Fearless Vampire Killers* (1967). On August 9, 1969, she and four others were murdered at the home she shared with Polanski by members of the Manson Family, a [[Cult]]. She was eight and a half months pregnant. Her last completed film, *12+1*, was released posthumously.

Removal of [[Hair|hair]] with a razor or other bladed implement, down to or near the skin. It is most commonly practiced by men to remove facial hair and by women to remove leg and underarm hair. Head shaving is associated with religious practice, the [[Military|armed forces]] and some competitive sports, and has been used to punish or to show submission. Copper razors were invented around 3000 BC. [[Alexander the Great]] promoted beard shaving for Macedonian soldiers, fearing enemies could grab them in battle. Straight razors have been made in [[Sheffield]], England, since the 18th century. King Camp Gillette invented the double-edged safety razor in 1895, and commercial production began in 1903. The razor grew popular during [[World War I]], when the U.S. military issued Gillette shaving kits to servicemen. Cancer patients often shave their heads when treatment causes hair loss.

Middle Eastern dish of meat cut into thin slices, stacked in an inverted cone and roasted on a slow-turning vertical spit. It originated in the [[Levant]] during the [[Ottoman Empire]]. Traditionally made with lamb or mutton, it may also use chicken, turkey, [[Beef|beef]] or veal, seasoned with spices such as [[Cumin|cumin]], [[Cardamom|cardamom]] and [[Turmeric|turmeric]]. The name derives from the Turkish *çevirme*, meaning "turning," which refers to rotisserie cooking. Lebanese immigrants brought the technique to Mexico in the early 20th century, where it led to tacos al pastor. In 2024 [[Ottawa]] City Council declared the city the "shawarma capital of Canada."

American retired professional wrestler, known as "the Heartbreak Kid." He wrestled for [[WWE]] (then the World Wrestling Federation) from 1988 until 1998, and again from 2002 until his 2010 retirement. He main-evented WrestleMania five times and co-founded the stable D-Generation X. Michaels held the WWF Championship three times and the WWE World Heavyweight Championship once, and he won the Royal Rumble twice. He was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2011 and again in 2019 with D-Generation X. He is regarded as one of the greatest professional wrestlers of all time.

Mathematical tool for tracking locally defined data, such as [[Abelian group|abelian groups]] or rings, attached to the [[Open set|open sets]] of a [[Topological space|topological space]]. For each open set the data might be the ring of continuous functions on it. Such data can be restricted to smaller open sets, and the data on an open set are equivalent to compatible data on a covering by smaller sets. The field that studies sheaves is called sheaf theory. Sheaves let geometric structures such as differentiable manifolds and schemes be described by sheaves of rings, and sheaf cohomology links topological and geometric properties. They also underpin D-modules, which apply to [[Differential equation|differential equations]], and have applications in [[Algebraic geometry|algebraic geometry]], [[Mathematical logic]] and [[Number theory]].

Ancient South Arabian kingdom in what is now [[Yemen]]. It likely began between c. 1000 BC and c. 800 BC. Its people, the Sabaeans, were central to South Arabian civilization for much of the 1st millennium BC, with a heartland around Marib. At times the kingdom extended across much of Yemen and into the [[Horn of Africa]], including [[Eritrea]] and [[Ethiopia]]. The first Sabaean kingdom, from the 8th to the 1st century BC, was dominant in South Arabia before a long decline. It re-emerged in the 1st to 3rd centuries CE, when a secondary capital was founded at Sanaa, and it ended around 275 CE in annexation by the Himyarites. The Sabaeans profited from the frankincense and myrrh trade and left many inscriptions. The [[Hebrew Bible]] account of the [[Queen of Sheba]] visiting [[Solomon]] is considered legendary.

City in [[Yorkshire|South Yorkshire]], [[England]], long known for [[Cutlery|cutlery]] and steel. It played a crucial role in the [[Industrial Revolution]], where processes for high-quality [[Stainless steel|stainless steel]] and crucible steel were invented in the 19th century. Its population grew almost tenfold, and it was granted city status in 1893. Decline in its iron, steel and coal industries in the 1970s and 1980s was followed by redevelopment. The city has more than 250 parks and woodlands. It is home to Sheffield F.C., the world's oldest football club, and to the World Snooker Championship. Musicians from the city include [[Def Leppard]] and the [[Arctic Monkeys]].

Bangladeshi politician and revolutionary, the founding president of [[Bangladesh]]. Born in Tungipara, he became a student activist in Bengal and joined the faction that became the Awami League in 1949. Leading the Awami League to victory in Pakistan's 1970 general election, he faced a military junta that refused to transfer power. Arrested by the Pakistan Army on March 25, 1971, he issued a proclamation of independence the next day, which marked the start of the [[Bangladesh Liberation War]]. He became prime minister in 1972, but economic mismanagement and the 1974 famine marked his rule. In 1975 he installed one-party rule and became effectively president for life, and he was assassinated in a coup that August. His legacy is divisive. Critics cite his economic failures, human rights abuses and authoritarianism, while most Bangladeshis credit him with independence.

American writer, cartoonist and songwriter, born and raised in [[Chicago]]. His cartoons appeared in [[Playboy]] during the 1950s, and he wrote the satirical *Uncle Shelby's ABZ Book*. His children's books include *The Giving Tree*, *Where the Sidewalk Ends* and *A Light in the Attic*. His works have been translated into more than 47 languages and have sold more than 20 million copies. As a songwriter, he wrote "A Boy Named Sue," recorded by [[Johnny Cash]] in 1969, which peaked at number 2 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100. He received two [[Grammy Awards]].

British multinational oil and gas company, headquartered in [[London]]. Formed in April 1907 by the merger of the Royal Dutch Petroleum Company of the [[Netherlands]] and the "Shell" Transport and Trading Company of the United Kingdom, it became the leading competitor of [[Standard Oil]] and by 1920 was the world's largest oil producer. It was one of the "Seven Sisters" that dominated the petroleum industry from the mid-1940s to the mid-1970s. Shell is vertically integrated, with operations in over 99 countries and a primary listing on the [[London Stock Exchange]]. Its revenue fell from $451 billion in 2013 to $284 billion in 2024.

[[Resin]] secreted by the female lac bug on trees in India and Thailand. Processed into flakes and dissolved in alcohol, it is used as a brush-on colorant, food glaze and [[Wood|wood]] finish, and as a primer and high-gloss varnish. Shellac was once used as an electrical insulator, and [[Phonograph|phonograph]] records were made of it until vinyl replaced it. From the 19th century it was a dominant wood finish in the Western world, until nitrocellulose lacquer largely replaced it in the 1920s and 1930s. It is also used as a candy glaze and to preserve harvested [[Citrus]] fruit.

American actress whose film career spanned seven decades. Born Shirley Schrift in [[St. Louis]], she changed her name to Shelley in 1943. She won two [[Academy Awards]], for *The Diary of Anne Frank* (1959) and *A Patch of Blue* (1965), and was nominated for *A Place in the Sun* (1951) and *The Poseidon Adventure* (1972). Her breakthrough came in *A Double Life* (1947), and she went on to appear in *The Night of the Hunter* (1955), *Lolita* (1962) and *Alfie* (1966). She played Nana Mary on the sitcom *Roseanne* and received a star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]] in 1960.

Sub-provincial city (pop., 2020: 9,070,093), formerly known as Mukden, and capital of Liaoning province in northeastern [[China]]. It was a stronghold of the [[Ming dynasty]], and in 1621 it briefly served as capital of the Jurchen Later Jin state, predecessor of the [[Qing dynasty]]. The 1905 Battle of Mukden, part of the [[Russo-Japanese War]], was fought south of the city. After the 1931 Mukden incident led to Japanese occupation of Manchuria, the city was part of the puppet state of [[Manchukuo]]. It remained a stronghold of the [[Kuomintang]] until Communist forces captured it in 1948. Shenyang is now an industrial center and the transportation and commercial hub of northeast China, with growing software, automotive and electronics industries. It is home to Northeastern University and Liaoning University.

Prefecture-level city (pop., 2025: 18.2 million) in [[Guangdong]], China. It was developed from a rural area into a city in 1979. [[Reform and opening up|Reform and opening up]], introduced by [[Deng Xiaoping]], made it China's first special economic zone in the early 1980s, owing to its proximity to [[Hong Kong]]. Foreign investment and migrants fueled rapid growth, and the city became a hub for technology, trade and finance. It is home to the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and is a global technology hub sometimes called China's [[Silicon Valley]]. Firms such as [[Huawei]] and [[Tencent]] are based there, and the city is the main home of BYD Company and the largest automobile manufacturing city in China.
